observations: Photo 0: A silver/black clamshell laptop, screen closed-ish but display dark/off, viewed from front-left angle on a white backdrop.
Photo 1: Close-up of open laptop keyboard area. Keys look physically intact, no visible cracks or missing keys.
Palm-rest stickers visible in photo 1: an Intel 'Core i5' logo, a 'Windows 7' logo, and an Energy Star sticker.
A barcode/serial sticker is visible at the top-right of the keyboard deck in photo 1 but the text is too small/blurred to read.
No visible brand or model text is legible on the lid or bezel in photo 0.
Screen is not shown powered on in either photo, so display condition cannot be judged.
No photos of the underside, ports, charger, or hinges are provided.

claims.evidence: No photo shows a battery test, charge indicator, or power-on state; claim is plausible but cannot be confirmed or contradicted from images.
No photo shows the screen powered on, no boot/BIOS screen, no port or hinge close-ups, so functional condition of screen, keyboard, trackpad, storage, and ports is unconfirmed.

risks.risk: Screen may be cracked, dim, or dead (not just the battery).
risks.proof: A photo or clip of the laptop powered on showing a clear, undistorted image on the full screen.
risks.if_unproven: priced as screen not working / unverified display

risks.risk: Battery condition may be worse than 'bad' (e.g., swollen, missing, or laptop won't run even on AC).
risks.proof: A clip showing the laptop powering on and running, plus a photo of the battery itself (health %, swelling) or a screenshot of battery status in OS.
risks.if_unproven: priced as battery requiring full replacement, worst case

risks.risk: Exact CPU generation, RAM size, and storage type/capacity are unknown, which materially changes value.
risks.proof: A screenshot of System Information / Task Manager / 'About this PC' showing CPU model, RAM, and storage.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest plausible spec for a 'Core i5, Windows 7-era' 15-inch laptop

risks.risk: Storage drive may be missing, faulty, or wiped.
risks.proof: A photo of the BIOS/boot screen or OS showing the drive detected and its capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced as storage not confirmed / possibly missing

risks.risk: Hidden physical damage (dents, cracked hinges, broken ports) not visible from the two angles shown.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the underside, all ports, and both hinges.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition unknown, assume moderate wear

risks.risk: Charger/adapter may not be included or may not match.
risks.proof: A photo of the original charger with model number plate.

proof_requests: Power-on video/photo showing the screen displaying an image clearly.
Screenshot of System Information (CPU model, RAM, storage) or BIOS screen.
Close-up photos of ports, hinges, and underside/base of the laptop.
Photo of the battery itself and/or a battery health screenshot.
Photo of the charger/adapter if included.
response.reason: The laptop's identity is only generic (Core i5 era, Windows 7 sticker) with no legible model, CPU generation, RAM, or storage shown, and the screen is never seen powered on, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without the missing specification and power-on proof.
